about.title: Walnut Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Walnut's crash reports show a steady, mid-week pattern — Wednesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. tend to see more reported collisions, often along Grand Avenue, Amar Road, Lemon Avenue, and La Puente Road. In the most recent full year on record, Los Angeles County logged 37 injury collisions in Walnut affecting 44 people, with no reported traffic deaths. Behind each of those numbers is someone dealing with medical bills, missed work, and a phone call from an insurance adjuster who wants a quick statement. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free connection service that puts you in touch with an independent attorney who can review your situation, explain your options under California law, and handle communication with the insurance company so you don't have to navigate it alone while you focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: Why Act Quickly After a Walnut Crash

items.title: California's Filing Deadline Is Firm
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like a public road agency — may be responsible. Waiting too long can close the door on your case entirely.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you were partly at fault for the crash, though your share of fault may reduce the amount. An attorney can help make sure fault is assessed fairly rather than assumed against you.

items.title: Don't Give the Other Insurer a Recorded Statement
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash, but what you say can be used to minimize your claim later. It's worth speaking with an attorney first, and preserving evidence like photos, witness names, and medical records while it's still fresh.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Walnut?
items.answer: Under California law, you typically have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your accident involved a government-owned road or vehicle, that deadline can shrink to as little as six months, so it's best not to wait to look into your options.

items.question: What if the crash happened on Grand Avenue or Amar Road and I was partly at fault?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility for the crash. Your recovery may be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't automatically eliminated. An attorney can help evaluate how fault applies to your specific situation.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in our network generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
